research_notes: The strict protocol intentionally treats successful incremental writes before target as neither pass nor failure.
This avoids survivorship bias from partial runs.
At the same time, incremental writes are valuable for diagnosing where a failed run stopped.
The final close record is therefore both a classification marker and a measurement of close overhead.
This dual role justifies keeping it small and stable across probes.
Future aggregation can use it as the canonical per-probe summary.
